steps.message:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Spain in October uses CEST (UTC+2). “5:00 PM ET” on September 30, 2026 corresponds to 11:00 PM UTC-?—specifically, Eastern Time in September 2026 is EDT (UTC−4), so 5:00 PM EDT = 21:00 UTC = 23:00 in Madrid (UTC+2).  

ANSWER: 2026-09-30 23:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Lima, Peru uses Peru Time (PET), which is UTC−5 year-round.  
July 15, 2026 at 12:00 UTC converts to 07:00 on July 15, 2026 in Lima.

ANSWER: 2026-07-15 07:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Applications are due June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CEST is UTC+2, while Tokyo (JST) is UTC+9, so Tokyo is 7 hours ahead of CEST.  
June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST → June 1, 2026 at 4:00 PM in Tokyo time.

ANSWER: 2026-06-01 16:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The contest ends on October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PDT in October is typically UTC−7. The deadline is **2026-10-11 23:59 PDT**, which is **2026-10-12 06:59 UTC**. Madrid in October is on CEST (UTC+2), so local time is **2026-10-12 08:59**.  

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 08:59 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PST (at that time of year) is UTC−08:00.  
March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST = March 4, 2026 at 07:59 UTC.  
Madrid in early March 2026 uses CET (UTC+01:00), so that is March 4, 2026 at 08:59 local time.

ANSWER: 2026-03-04 08:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "Deadline: 10:00 AM CET, February 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Los Angeles uses Pacific Time. On February 2, 2026, Los Angeles is on PST (UTC−8), while CET is UTC+1, so the difference is 9 hours.  
10:00 AM CET on 2026-02-02 becomes 1:00 AM PST on 2026-02-02.

ANSWER: 2026-02-02 01:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submit by 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

JST is UTC+9. Lima, Peru is UTC-5 year-round. So the difference is 14 hours (JST is 14 hours ahead of Lima).  

8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026 → 6:00 PM on May 4, 2026 in Lima local time.  

ANSWER: 2026-05-04 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is on Central European Summer Time in late October 2026? Actually Spain switches to standard time (CET, UTC+1) on the last Sunday of October, and in 2026 that falls on **October 25**—so by **October 28, 2026** Madrid is on **CET (UTC+1)**.

“11:59 PM PT” is **23:59 Pacific Time**. In October, PT is typically **PDT (UTC−7)**, so convert to UTC: 23:59 + 7 hours = **06:59 UTC** on October 29, 2026. Convert UTC to Madrid time (UTC+1): 06:59 + 1 hour = **07:59** on **October 29, 2026**.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 07:59 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The live session starts October 30, 2026, 9:00 AM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid in late October uses Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2).  
“9:00 AM ET” on 2026-10-30 is Eastern Time, which is UTC-4 in late October, so 9:00 AM ET = 13:00 UTC. Converting to Madrid (UTC+2) gives 15:00 local time.  

ANSWER: 2026-10-30 15:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in New York, USA. A contest page says: "Voting closes October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET is Central European Time (UTC+1). New York observes Eastern Time: in October 2026 it will be on Eastern Daylight Time (EDT), UTC-4.  
So the time difference is 5 hours (CET is 5 hours ahead of EDT).  

October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET → October 27, 2026 at 13:00 EDT (local time in New York).  

ANSWER: 2026-10-27 13:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Final round closes November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

“PT” refers to Pacific Time. On **November 2, 2026**, Madrid is on **CET (UTC+1)**, while Pacific Time is on **PST (UTC−8)** (no daylight saving in effect in early November), so the time difference is **9 hours**.

11:59 PM PT on Nov 2, 2026 → **next day** at 08:59 AM in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-11-03 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid uses Central European Summer Time (CEST) in March, which is UTC+2. “11:59 PM PT” refers to Pacific Time in that date range (likely PDT, UTC−7). So the time difference is 9 hours, making it 08:59 on March 21, 2026 in Madrid.  

ANSWER: 2026-03-21 08:59 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "The webinar starts March 25, 2026, 12:00 PM CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Los Angeles is in Pacific Time in March 2026: PDT (UTC−7) starts March 8, 2026. CET is UTC+1, so the time difference is 8 hours (CET ahead of LA). Therefore, 12:00 PM CET on March 25, 2026 is 4:00 AM PDT on March 25, 2026 in Los Angeles.

ANSWER: 2026-03-25 04:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

“12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026” means midnight at the start of October 12, 2026 in Eastern Time. In Madrid, Spain, on that date Spain observes CEST (UTC+2) and Eastern Time is in EDT (UTC-4), so the difference is +6 hours. Therefore, midnight ET corresponds to 06:00 in Madrid on October 12, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 06:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Papers are due October 9, 2026 (23:59 AoE)."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

“AoE” means Anywhere on Earth, which corresponds to UTC−12 (the last time zone used worldwide). Madrid in October uses Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2.  
So the deadline “October 9, 2026 23:59 AoE” is the same instant as “October 10, 2026 17:59” in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-10 17:59 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Registration closes 12:00 PM PT, August 14, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

“12:00 PM PT” on **August 14, 2026** depends on whether PT means Pacific Time (most commonly **Pacific Daylight Time** in August, UTC−7). Madrid in August uses **Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2)**.  

So the time difference is **9 hours** ahead in Madrid (UTC+2 minus UTC−7 = 9). Therefore, **12:00 PT** corresponds to **21:00 (9:00 PM) in Madrid** on the same date.

ANSWER: 2026-08-14 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 11:59 PM IST, November 10, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

IST is UTC+5:30. Madrid in November is on Central European Time (CET, UTC+1). So the difference is +4 hours 30 minutes (IST is 4:30 hours ahead of Madrid). Therefore, 11:59 PM IST on 2026-11-10 converts to 7:29 PM CET on 2026-11-10.  

ANSWER: 2026-11-10 19:29

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submissions close at 5:00 PM Nepal time on April 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Nepal time is UTC+5:45. Lima, Peru is UTC-5 (in April 2026, Peru is on standard time, no DST).  
So Nepal is 10 hours 45 minutes ahead of Lima.  

5:00 PM on April 2, 2026 (Nepal time) → 6:15 AM on April 2, 2026 (Lima time).  

ANSWER: 2026-04-02 06:15

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Applications close 10:00 AM Adelaide time, October 6, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Adelaide, Australia uses Australian Central Daylight Time (ACDT, UTC+10:30) in early October. Madrid, Spain in October is on Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2). The time difference is therefore 8 hours 30 minutes.

So, **10:00 AM Adelaide time on October 6, 2026** = **01:30 AM Madrid time on October 6, 2026**.

ANSWER: 2026-10-06 01:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close 6:00 PM Sydney time on October 3, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Sydney time in October 3, 2026 is AEST (UTC+10). Madrid in October is CEST (UTC+2). The difference is 8 hours, with Sydney ahead of Madrid, so subtract 8 hours from 6:00 PM.

6:00 PM (Sydney) on 2026-10-03 → 10:00 AM (Madrid) on 2026-10-03.

ANSWER: 2026-10-03 10:00
